headline: Nasdaq enters correction as chip rout deepens before Nvidia's first results since Huang's exit
subhead: The S&P 500 fell 1.9 percent to 7,416.6 and the Nasdaq 2.5 percent, Nvidia dropped 4.1 percent to a 52-week low of 156.14, and the VIX jumped 18.7 percent to 22.9.

us.text: S&P 500 fell 1.9 percent to 7,416.6 and the Nasdaq 2.5 percent, now 11.2 percent below its 52-week high; chip index lost 5.3 percent.
Nvidia fell 4.1 percent to a 52-week low of 156.14 after Huang's resignation and a new US rule on China's AI chip access; results due Tuesday.
Treasury yields dipped, the 10-year to 5.12 percent, as Fed Chair Warsh warned AI might disappoint; futures price a 95.7 percent chance of a December hike.

india.text: Nifty rose 146.8 points to 25,291.10 and Sensex 510.4 points to 82,102.85 on Monday, led by banks and FMCG; the price feed here still shows Friday.
FIIs net bought 4,865 crore rupees in cash on Monday, an 11th straight buying session, while DIIs net sold 3,519 crore.
Rupee rose 27 paise to close at 93.92 per dollar on foreign inflows and softer crude.

global.text: Kospi closed Monday at 5,100.25 as SK hynix and Samsung slid, Nikkei finished below 60,000, and both fell again at Tuesday's open.
STOXX 600 closed at 662.31, snapping a five-session record run as AI caution weighed on tech and miners; Hang Seng rose to 23,753.84.
Brent settled at 92.44 dollars and WTI at 85.72 as Hormuz flows recovered; bitcoin touched 62,100 at the weekend, its lowest since July.

weekly.narrative: Jensen Huang's sudden exit as Nvidia CEO dominated the week: Nvidia fell 12.8 percent, but rotation into Apple, AMD and Broadcom still left the S&P 500 up 2.5 percent and the Nasdaq up 2.3 percent despite a Friday AI selloff. Hot US CPI and 6.5 percent annual PPI pushed the 10-year yield to 5.15 percent and left a December Fed hike fully priced, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high. That weighed on metals and crypto: gold fell 4.5 percent to a 13-month low, silver 6.1 percent and bitcoin broke below 70,000 dollars. India leaned on nine straight sessions of foreign buying and a bank rally, though the Nifty slipped to 25,144.3 on Friday after October CPI rose to 6.09 percent. Next week brings Nvidia results on 17 November, FOMC minutes on 18 November and Anthropic's expected Nasdaq debut on 19 November.
